TRAFFIC ADVISORY: @caltransdist3 plans to close the westbound U.S. Route 50 off-ramp at Jefferson Boulevard today, April 19, from 6:00 AM until 3:00 PM. This closure is expected to significantly impact fans traveling to Sutter Health Park for the Sacramento Athletics vs. Chicago White Sox day game (first pitch at 1:05 PM).

Fans planning to attend the game should use one of the following recommended routes:

🚙Option 1 (via Downtown Sacramento / Tower Bridge): Motorists should utilize Interstate 5 and exit at J Street. Continue southbound on 3rd Street, then proceed westbound on Capitol Avenue acrossTower Bridge into West Sacramento. From there, access parking via Riverfront Street or 5th Street.

🚗Option 2 (via Harbor Blvd / SR-275): Motorists traveling westbound on Highway 50 should exit at Harbor Boulevard and proceed south over the freeway. Re-enter Highway 50 eastbound and take the Jefferson Boulevard / Downtown Sacramento exit (#3). Continue ontoCabaldon Parkway toward the stadium, then access parking via 5th Street or Riverfront Street.

Please drive safely!

data.raw_text:
a Renaissance Technologies researcher found me through a mutual friend and asked to "audit" my terminal

we met at a wine bar in the west village. he wouldn't order anything, said he was working.
                                                      
"show me the infrastructure"

i opened the laptop. terminal was live. +$31,204 running 9 weeks.

he didn't look at the P&L. he looked at the signal stack.
"this is 8 orthogonal detectors running in parallel with a consensus gate, who wrote this"

Claude Opus 4.7, one weekend, one repo.

https://t.co/3R5zEcC8PT

2,900 stars. 36GB. every trade on Polymarket since launch, every wallet, every resolution.

i gave Claude one prompt at 10pm on a friday: "read this entire dataset. find every wallet with >80% win rate across 200+ trades. reverse engineer their edge. build a detector for each pattern"

by sunday 6am the terminal was live.

he went through the code for 40 minutes. didn't speak.

then: "three of your detectors match papers we haven't published yet"

i asked which ones.

he wouldn't say.

8 detectors running:

> entropy collapse
> mempool topology
> oracle propagation
> wallet cryo freeze
> cluster accumulation
> flow pressure delta
> disposition filter
> conviction decay

enters when 3+ fire on the same market. exits when consensus drops below 2.

last 6 weeks:

> Iran deal vote +$1,048
> BTC 220K Q2 +$1,217
> Fed emergency cut +$892
> Typhoon CAT5 Philippines +$934
> TSLA robotaxi launch +$1,311
> Lunar gateway slip +$871
> Saudi IPO delay +$763
> AAPL vision 2 launch +$692

1,043 trades. 83% win rate. sharpe 3.27. kelly f+ 0.104. avg hold 4h31m. worst drawdown -1.8%.

+$31,204 from $1,800 seed.

he closed the laptop himself.

"we have a 22 person team doing what this does. we started in 2019."

i told him i started friday night.

trading here: https://t.co/IEU82UZaxz

he paid for my wine on the way out. we hadn't ordered any.

data.raw_text:
Walk through the outskirts of Kampala,Manila, or Mumbai & you’ll see it:mountains of plastic waste smoldering under a brutal sun.Children play nearby.Mothers breathe toxic smoke. Rivers run thick with discarded bottles,bags, and wrappers  the same ones that glowed under supermarket lights just weeks before.

Every single minute,one million plastic bottles are sold around the world.That’s 1.5 billion per day. Less than 9% of all plastic ever produced has been recycled. The rest?It is burned in open pits, buried in illegal dumps,shredded into microplastics that drift into our lungs & blood or shipped thousands of miles to become someone else’s crisis.

But let’s be clear:plastic pollution is not a littering problem. It is not a personal failing of the poor. It is a justice problem  engineered by the same corporations that promised us recycling was the answer while quietly doubling down on single-use production.

Oil and gas giants are racing to build hundreds of new plastic plants,mostly in low-income communities and communities of color.They know plastic is a lifeline for fossil fuels as the world moves away from burning coal and oil. And they know that once that bottle,wrapper or sachet leaves your hand,the cost of dealing with it falls on the rest of us especially on the Global South.

From Uganda to Indonesia, communities already on the frontlines of climate breakdown are now drowning in plastic.Their soil turns barren.Their water sources clog and poison.Their children suffer from asthma, cancer, and birth defects at alarming rates.Meanwhile, the brands behind the waste  Coca-Cola, PepsiCo,Nestlé, Unilever continue to market their products as “recyclable” & “eco-friendly,”knowing full well that most recycling infrastructure doesn’t exist where it’s needed most.

We cannot recycle our way out of this.Recycling was never designed to handle the scale of today’s plastic flood.Less than 10% of global plastic gets a second life.The rest is a death sentence for ecosystems & frontline communities.

That is why we need systemic change not just better habits,but binding rules and real accountability.

1. A Global Plastics Treaty with real production caps. 
The UN is negotiating a treaty right now. But industry lobbyists are fighting hard to keep it voluntary and weak.We need mandatory reductions in virgin plastic production,a phase-out of the most dangerous chemicals & an end to waste colonialism where rich countries dump their trash on poorer nations.

2. Corporate accountability for single-use plastics.  
Brands that choose convenience over the planet must pay for the full lifecycle of their packaging. That means Extended Producer Responsibility laws that are actually enforced not just greenwashed press releases. If a company sells a bottle,it must ensure that bottle never becomes a poison pill for a community thousands of miles away.

3. Investment in zero-waste systems led by frontline communities.
The people who have lived with the crisis longest know the solutions best.Waste pickers, youth organizers,Indigenous leaders  they are already building community-led composting, reuse networks & repair cafes.They need funding,not photo ops.They need power,not pity.

The grassroots are not waiting. From the Break Free From Plastic movement to young climate strikers across Africa and Asia, people power is already building a different world.We are refilling, repairing,reusing, & demanding less plastic in the first place.

It’s time for leaders to catch up. It’s time for a treaty that prioritizes people over profit. It’s time to stop calling landfills“waste management” & start calling them what they are:monuments to broken systems.@ahengst
